# Agreed Scope for v2.0.0

**Status**: Implementation and static review complete on `codex/feat/v2-context-optimization`; v2.0.0 publication authorized by the project owner.

This is an upstream maintainer scope record. The implementation changes the v2
workflow; published v1 releases remain unchanged.

## Required Deliverables

- Integrate the general context optimization into the default instruction,
  delivery, role, and adapter structure. New projects must receive the optimized
  structure directly, without running a separate optimization prompt.
- Add `howto/context-optimization.md` explaining the rationale, responsibility
  boundaries, task-dependent context loading, migration approach, and checks.
- Add `howto/prompts/context-optimization.md` containing a reusable AI migration
  prompt linked to the guide.
- Add `howto/upgrades/v1-to-v2.md` describing the affected files, required changes,
  preservation of project customizations, verification, and version recording
  for existing v1 projects.
- Link the guide and upgrade path from the root README and relevant delivery
  documentation.

## Source Material and Constraints

Use the AppRelay documents `delivery-system-kontextoptimierung.md` and
`delivery-system-kontextoptimierung-prompt.md` as source material. Adapt them
rather than copying their project-specific paths or assumptions.

- Write all files in English.
- Preserve security and approval gates, project-specific rules, existing user
  changes, and the optional delivery diagnostics setting.
- Keep canonical rules in the default instruction files; guides explain and
  reference those rules rather than maintaining competing definitions.
- Treat reduced context size as an optimization goal, not a guarantee that a
  particular context window will be sufficient.
- Verify tool-specific formats and behavior before claiming compatibility.
- Do not overwrite completed project documents or relocate existing
  documentation roots as part of a routine upgrade.

## Release Acceptance

v2.0.0 is not ready for publication until the optimized default, rationale and
how-to, reusable prompt, and v1 upgrade path are implemented, consistent with one
another, and reviewed. Verification must cover both new-project bootstrap and
existing-project migration, including preservation of project rules and gates.

Implementation was explicitly authorized by the project owner after v1.1.0.
The project owner subsequently authorized committing, pushing, and publishing
v2.0.0 with the documented live-test limitations. See [verification evidence](v2.0.0-verification.md)
for completed checks and deferred live-tool validation.
